source.title: Geometric SSM: LTI State Space Models for Selective Tasks
source.authors: Umberto Casti; Giacomo Baggio; Sandro Zampieri; Fabio Pasqualetti

page_placements.theme: Induction-style recall and copying in non-attention and hybrid architectures

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates induction-task accuracy in state-space models, but does not identify or measure attention heads, their formation, or in-context learning as described in the claim versions. Its results are related to induction behavior but do not test a version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy on standard and extended induction-head tasks. These results measure task performance in state-space models, not induction heads or their formation, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The sequential MNIST result does not bear on the claim and is omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper uses the synthetic induction-head task (Fu et al.; Gu & Dao) only as a benchmark for its own Geometric SSM against an isolated Mamba selective layer. Both models are trained directly on the task, so the behaviour is induced on purpose, not observed arising. No attention heads, head composition, training dynamics or token-index loss are measured. The results show task accuracy, not whether induction heads form (V1, V2, V4, V5, V7) or carry in-context learning (V3, V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct; it should add the authors' central claim. They argue, contra Gu & Dao, that selectivity does not require time-varying dynamics: LTI systems built with geometric control can be selective. On synthetic tasks the Geometric SSM reaches 0.99+ accuracy. The small Selective SSM degrades with sequence length and fails the extended task (below 20%), which they attribute to its memoryless selection. They also note the gap with Mamba's reported perfect accuracy may reflect model capacity (74K vs 700 parameters).
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates synthetic induction-task accuracy in state-space models; does not reproduce measurements of attention-head mechanisms, training-time formation, or token-index loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported task accuracy varies with sequence length and with model/task setting: the Selective SSM's accuracy declines at longer lengths, while the Geometric SSM remains at 0.99+ in the reported ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: On the standard induction-head task, the 50-parameter Geometric SSM scores 0.99+ validation accuracy at lengths 2^4 to 2^10. The roughly 700-parameter single-layer Selective SSM falls from 0.70 to 0.20 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When trained directly on the synthetic induction task, an LTI Geometric SSM length-generalizes near-perfectly, while a small single-layer Mamba selective layer does not.

fits_no_version.finding: On the extended task with a 4-token trigger, the Geometric SSM scores 0.99+ at all lengths. The Selective SSM falls from 0.69 to 0.13, which the authors attribute to Mamba's memoryless, current-input-only selection (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-token-trigger induction requires a selection mechanism with temporal memory, which Mamba's input-only selection lacks.

record.problems: The evidence is from synthetic tasks rather than foundation models. The authors describe their single-layer models as substantially smaller than the cited Mamba setup. No uncertainty estimates or explicit control results are reported for the induction-task tables.
record.rows_left_out: The sequential MNIST test accuracy comparison (Section 4.5, Table 4) is outside the claim's subject and is omitted.

untested.parts: No attention-only transformers, previous-token heads or head composition are studied.
No training trajectory, abrupt formation, in-context-learning gain or loss bump is reported.
No large transformers and no loss-versus-token-index measure.
SSMs are trained directly on the induction task. Whether induction-like mechanisms emerge in other architectures during ordinary training is not tested.
Training data and setup are not varied to see when induction mechanisms form.
No few-shot task learning and no comparison of mechanisms.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4: the induction task is a tool for benchmarking the authors' own architecture. All rows compare the study's own method with a baseline method and bear on no version; keep versions ['none']. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the Selective SSM is a deliberately shrunken single layer, so its low scores do not reflect full Mamba. The sMNIST omission is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: No attention heads, previous-token heads, head composition, or head-level copying mechanism are measured.
No training trajectory, onset of induction heads, in-context-learning transition, or training-loss bump is measured.
No large transformers or token-index loss measure of in-context learning is studied.
The paper evaluates induction-task performance in state-space models, but does not test whether heads with induction behavior occur across model families, sizes, or runs.
No comparison of data or training setups for induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning is made.
No few-shot task learning or comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms is measured.
No stages or sub-steps in induction-head formation are measured.

relation.reason: Evaluates synthetic recall accuracy, without measuring attention-head composition, spontaneous formation, training transitions, or token-index loss.

tranche.reason: Uses the induction-head task as a benchmark for its own selection architecture; reports task-trained SSM performance without testing any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 10 March 2026. Results compare small single-layer models using an isolated Mamba selective component; they do not establish induction-head mechanisms or full Mamba performance.
